title: The bee
hook: your Lord inspired the bee to build, to eat, to make honey with healing in it (16:68–69)

segments.voice: Yesterday: milk between, pure milk from between waste and blood. Your line was pure from between.

Somewhere a jar of honey sits on a kitchen shelf, the work of a crowd you'll never meet, flying back and forth over fields you'll never see. Surah sixteen is named after that crowd. An-Nahl: the Bee. Of all the creatures in its long list of gifts, the bee gets the name on the cover, and two verses all its own.

Verse sixty-eight begins, in Pickthall's words: "And thy Lord inspired the bee". The verb is awha, from the same root as wahy, the word for revelation, used when God speaks to prophets. Elsewhere the Qur'an uses it for the quiet prompting given to the mother of Musa. And here, for an insect. Commentators usually explain it as instinct, a guidance placed inside the creature, but they keep the word: the bee is guided. Then three instructions. Make your homes in the hills, in the trees, and in what people build for you. Eat from every kind of fruit. And follow the ways of your Lord, made smooth for you. Arabic grammarians point out that these commands are in the feminine form. Then verse sixty-nine: from their bellies comes a drink of many colors, with healing in it for people. Anyone who's seen pale clover honey next to dark buckwheat knows the many colors. The verse ends: this is a sign for people who reflect. A story in Sahih al-Bukhari shows how seriously the companions took it. A man came to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and said his brother's stomach was troubling him. Give him honey, the Prophet said. The man came back: no better. Honey, again. Back again, no better. Honey, a third time. When the man returned once more, the Prophet said: God has spoken the truth and your brother's stomach is wrong; give him honey. He did, and his brother recovered. Muslims read the verse as a sign, and some keep honey in the kitchen as a remedy. The verse names it a healing, not the only one.
screen: `AWHA: THE BEE IS GUIDED.` · `BUILD, EAT, FOLLOW THE SMOOTH WAYS.` · `A DRINK OF MANY COLORS.` · `HONEY, AGAIN, AND AGAIN.` · then, large: `HEALING IN IT FOR PEOPLE.`

segments.voice: If you have honey, put a little on a spoon; if not, anything sweet will do, or just remember the taste. Look at its color, one of honey's many, then taste it slowly and let it sit. For the rest of the sit, think of one thing that heals you, a person, a walk, a song, and if you pray, say alhamdulillah for it.
The bee. Guided by the same word as revelation, told to build, eat and follow smooth paths, and giving a drink of many colors with healing in it. Today's word.
Your line: healing in it. A drink of many colors, guided from the start. Day four hundred fifty-three, done.

It means the bee received a scripture, just as the prophets did.
It's a poetic flourish; the word has no tie to revelation at all.
